summary: Aroostook County, ME: 24-ft steel tower from 1914 with a watchman's house; now removed, but a land-trust trail reaches the summit, where one blog describes tower anchor points.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower is no longer standing; Forest Lookouts marks it removed without a date; one blog describes dismantled tower anchor points at the summit

access.note: Hedgehog Mountain Land Trust lists the summit trail as a hiking trail; no closure found in the sources read

visit.trail_note: About 0.75 miles, steep, from a trailhead at a rest area on the west side of ME-11; one blog calls the trail unmarked

events.note: Forestry department erected a 24-foot steel tower on the mountain
A 12-by-14-foot watchman's house built at the foot of the mountain beside a spring
Trail cleared from camp to the lookout station
Station repaired, painted and put in good condition, per the chief warden for the Fish River territory (J.M. Brown)
Maine Forest Service 360-degree panoramic map centred on the Hedgehog Mt. fire tower in Township 15 Range 6
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

notes_for_editor: The remains at the summit (cabin and anchor points) rest on one blog post, not on a land trust, Forest Service or register source. The register says only that the tower is no longer standing. Trail length is 0.75 miles in Maine Trail Finder and about 0.7 miles in the blog. Township 15 Range 6 WELS agrees across the Forest Lookouts page and the 1919 DigitalMaine map. Nothing found on whether the land is in public or private ownership beyond the trail listing; the Hedgehog Mountain Land Trust could confirm the summit's status. No photo entry: the DigitalMaine map has no image URL retrieved.
